newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy senate approves three-year economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Italy senate approves three-year economic plan.

text.p: Italy's Senate (upper house of parliament) on Tuesday approved the centre-left government's three-year programme of key economic targets (DPEF).
The voting was 114 for, eight abstentions from hard-left Communist Refoundation, and 16 against. The lower house has already approved the plan 282 votes to 158.
The programme sets out strict targets for 1998-2000 to keep Italy on track to join Europe's planned economic and monetary union at its 1999 launch.
Communist Refoundation, which holds the balance of power in the lower house, voted in favour of the DPEF there to ensure its passage but had announced it would abstain in the senate.

The DPEF targets an ambitious 1998 deficit-to-Gross Domestic Product ratio of 2.8 percent after planned deficit cuts of 25 trillion lire. The ratio is below the important three percent threshold set for aspiring EMU members.
